sections.h2: What is a mechanic's lien on a Florida home?
sections.html:
It is a claim against the property by someone who supplied labor, services or materials and was not paid. Florida calls it a construction lien, and Chapter 713 of the Florida Statutes sets who can file one and how.

A lien attaches to the real property, not just to the contractor, which is why it shows up in a title search when the owner tries to sell. A lienor who is not in privity with the owner, such as a subcontractor, supplier or sub-subcontractor, can still claim against the home under section 713.06 if the lienor follows the notice steps. The total of all liens for work under one direct contract may not exceed the contract price, with limited exceptions.

sections.h2: What deadlines control a Florida construction lien?
sections.html:
The claim of lien must be recorded no later than 90 days after the lienor's final furnishing of labor, services or materials, under section 713.08(5). It is recorded in the clerk's office, and in each county if the property spans more than one.

A lienor who is not in privity with the owner has an earlier step. Section 713.06(2)(a) requires a notice to owner before starting, or no later than 45 days after starting, to furnish labor, services or materials, and in any event before the owner's final payment after the contractor's affidavit. Failure to serve it, or to serve it on time, is a complete defense to enforcement of the lien. Laborers are excused from that notice.

  • Notice to owner: before starting or within 45 days after starting.
  • Claim of lien recorded: within 90 days after final furnishing.
  • Claim of lien served on the owner: before recording or within 15 days after, or the claim is voidable to the extent the delay prejudiced someone.
  • Suit to enforce: within 1 year of recording the claim.

sections.h2: What must a recorded claim of lien say?
sections.html:
Section 713.08 requires the lienor to state its name and service address, who it contracted with, the labor or materials and their price or value, a legal description, the owner's name, the first and last dates of work, and the amount unpaid.

The claim must be signed and sworn, and it must carry a statutory warning that the lien may remain valid for one year from recording and then expire unless legal proceedings have begun. Errors do not automatically void it. A court can still enforce a lien against someone who was not adversely affected by an omission or mistake, and a claim can be amended while the recording period is still open. Ask a Florida attorney to read the recorded claim against this list, since defects are a common basis for contesting a lien.

sections.h2: How long does the lien last, and how can an owner shorten it?
sections.html:
A lien ends one year after the claim is recorded, unless an action to enforce it has started in court within that time. Section 713.22 sets that period, and a recorded amended claim that shows a later final furnishing date restarts the year.

An owner or the owner's attorney can shorten the time by recording a Notice of Contest of Lien. The lienor then has 60 days from service of the notice to sue, and the lien is extinguished automatically if it does not. The clerk serves the notice on the lienor at the address shown in the claim and records it, and the clerk charges fees for those services.

Even a lien that lives past the year through a filed suit is not enforceable against creditors or later purchasers for value without notice unless a lis pendens is recorded. That detail is part of why title companies check the court docket as well as the property records.

sections.h2: How do you remove a lien so the house can sell?
sections.html:
Section 713.21 lists five ways: a satisfaction entered in the clerk's record, a signed and recorded release, the lienor's failure to sue in time, a court order after a show-cause hearing, or a recorded final judgment.

  1. Pay the lienor and record a notarized satisfaction or release that cites the official records reference number and recording date of the lien.
  2. Wait out the one-year period if no suit was filed, or shorten it with a Notice of Contest.
  3. File a complaint in circuit court. The clerk issues a summons telling the lienor to show cause within 20 days why the lien should not be enforced by action or canceled.
  4. Record a certified judgment showing the final outcome of any enforcement case.

A closing agent can often pay a lien from proceeds if the lienor gives a payoff figure and a release. Recording the release costs clerk fees under section 28.24, starting at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, plus the trust fund and technology charges listed there.

sections.h2: Does a lien come before a mortgage?
sections.html:
Priority depends on recording dates. Under section 713.07, a direct contractor's lien attaches and takes priority as of the time the notice of commencement is recorded, or the claim of lien if no notice was recorded.

Any conveyance, encumbrance or demand recorded before that attach date takes priority over the lien, along with its proceeds regardless of when disbursed. Liens of those not in privity under sections 713.03 and 713.04 attach at recording of the claim. This is why a mortgage recorded before the notice of commencement generally stands ahead, and one recorded afterward may not.

sections.h2: What can a homeowner do to avoid paying twice?
sections.html:
Get written releases each time you pay the contractor, and hold the final payment until the contractor's final payment affidavit arrives. The statutory notice to owner itself warns that unpaid suppliers may lien the property even if the owner paid the contractor in full.

Under section 713.06(3)(d), the contractor must give the owner a sworn affidavit listing any unpaid lienors, and the owner retains the final payment until it is delivered. The contractor must deliver it at least 5 days before suing to enforce a lien. An owner who fails to withhold can remain liable for valid liens of which the owner has notice. For a sale, ask the title company early what it sees on the record.

faqs.q: How long do I have to record a mechanic's lien in Florida?
faqs.a: A lienor must record the claim within 90 days after final furnishing of labor, services or materials, under section 713.08(5). Lienors outside a direct contract with the owner must also serve a notice to owner on time, or the lien can be defeated.

faqs.q: How long does a Florida construction lien last?
faqs.a: One year after the claim is recorded, unless an enforcement suit begins in that time. Section 713.22 also lets an owner record a Notice of Contest that gives the lienor 60 days to sue or lose the lien.

faqs.q: Can I sell my house with a mechanic's lien on it?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but the buyer's title company will want the lien paid, released or otherwise cleared at closing. Ask the lienor for a payoff and a recordable release, or use one of the discharge methods in section 713.21.

faqs.q: Does the lienor have to tell me it filed a lien?
faqs.a: Yes. The claim of lien must be served on the owner. Under section 713.08(4)(c), failing to serve it before recording or within 15 days after makes it voidable to the extent that the delay prejudiced someone.

faqs.q: What is a notice of commencement?
faqs.a: It is the owner's recorded notice for a construction project. Under section 713.07, a direct contractor's lien takes priority as of its recording, or as of the claim of lien if no notice was recorded.
